title: Build the FPL Benchmark Kernel
description:
## What to build

Turn the current Phase 1 scaffolding into a reproducible benchmark kernel for comparing deterministic analytics, optimisation, evidence agents and human decisions under identical point-in-time information.

The kernel must create immutable deadline episodes, execute policy arms under explicit budgets, validate and freeze proposals before outcome reveal, preserve longitudinal policy state, and report paired decision quality, calibration, safety, cost and latency. It must keep browser execution deferred and source collection governed.

Files: docs/evaluation/benchmark-protocol.md, control/schemas/benchmark/**, src/orchestration/**, src/evaluation/**, evals/episodes/**, tests/**
design:
Kernel contract: immutable episode manifest -> arm runner -> deterministic validation -> frozen proposal/GDR -> hidden-outcome reveal -> longitudinal transition -> paired and clustered evaluation.

Required arms: naive baseline; forecast plus optimiser; constrained evidence agent; evidence agent plus challenger; human decision. Historical replay is primary for structured-data arms. Live paired shadow evaluation is primary for evidence-dependent arms.

Every run records episode and snapshot IDs, source hashes, code commit, rules/model/prompt/tool versions, resource budgets, JSONL trace, validation, proposal, outcome, cost, latency, safety events and degraded-mode decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Child beads collectively implement the episode contract, genuine replay, longitudinal state, agent arms and evaluation.
- No arm can observe hidden outcomes before its proposal is frozen.
- Every comparison is paired on the same observed episode and reports uncertainty plus resource use.
- Collection remains source-registry gated and browser execution remains deferred.
